newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs tumble on EIAs, weak crude futures.
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs tumble on EIAs, weak crude futures.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices tumbled on Thursday under the weight of bearish stock data and sagging NYMEX crude oil futures, players said.
According to the latest Energy Information Administration report late Wednesday, propane stocks grew by 7.4 million barrels last month to 47.5 million, which is 17 percent above year-ago levels.

The EIA said if inventories continue to build at normal rates for the remainder of the stock building season, U.S. stocks may reach 60 million barrels by the start of the 1997-8 heating season, the highest pre-heating season level since 1994.
Augmenting the bearishness was weaker NYMEX crude oil futures, down on news that Germany was expected to raise 400 million marks this year from oil reserve sales.
In the Midwest, Conway, Kansas, spot propane traded at 33.75 cents a gallon, about 0.75 cent below Wednesday. U.S. Gulf Coast material swapped hands at 34.25 cents, a half cent below Wednesday.
The butane markets were also weaker, down a quarter to 39.75 cents in Belvieu and down a quarter in Conway. -- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
